title: The Trail of Cape Reckoning
premise: Bush pilot Xanthe Okafor hauls a river-drowned chest into his floatplane and finds it stamped with the seal of Vessania, a nation erased from every map forty years ago. Inside are letters proving his late mother was heir to a hidden colony's treasury—and that the men who 'resettled' Vessania have been hunting her bloodline ever since. Pursued by a government surveyor who is more than he claims, Xanthe flies and paddles upriver toward the forbidden source where survivors of the drowned nation still keep faith with old promises. At Cape Reckoning he must choose between surrendering the inheritance to buy peace for the settlement or exposing the truth that will burn his own name down. He chooses truth, loses the chest, and gains something rarer: a people, a partner, and a home no map can erase.
about_author: H. M. Voss is the pen name of a former northern freight pilot who logged a decade of river runs before trading the cockpit for a writing desk. Their fiction draws on real backwater airstrips, half-buried colonial histories, and the stubborn communities the maps forgot.

chapters.title: Weather Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Xanthe Okafor runs medicine and gossip up the Kestrel River in his aging floatplane, dodging a storm and a debt to the airfield owner. POV: Xanthe. Beat: establish his self-imposed invisibility and the quiet ache of a man avoiding his own history.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Low water after the storm exposes a bronze-bound chest on a gravel bar. Xanthe hauls it aboard against his better judgment; inside, sealed letters bear the seal of Vessania, a nation struck from maps in his childhood. POV: Xanthe. Beat: curiosity overriding caution—the hook sets.

chapters.title: The Surveyor at Mile Nine
chapters.summary: A government surveyor named Aldous Crane charting 'flood damage' books a ride and asks too many precise questions about salvage law. Xanthe lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. POV: Xanthe. Beat: first shadow of pursuit; reader senses Crane knows about the chest.

chapters.title: Letters in a Dead Hand
chapters.summary: Deciphering the letters by lamplight, Xanthe recognizes his mother's handwriting: she was born Vessani, an heir, and fled with documents naming the treasury's location at the river's source. POV: alternating Xanthe and letter excerpts. Beat: grief and vertigo—his whole exile was built on her silence.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Xanthe visits archivist Miriam Sable in the river town of Corben's Landing, who confirms Vessania was dissolved by emergency decree and its records burned—except what families smuggled out. She warns him someone else has been asking. POV: Miriam briefly, then Xanthe. Beat: the past has living enemies.

chapters.title: Crane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe catches Crane photographing his logbook and confronts him; Crane offers money for the chest, then a veiled threat about Xanthe's airworthiness certificates. POV: Xanthe. Beat: duty versus survival crystallizes—he can't stay invisible anymore.

chapters.title: The Pilot Who Waited
chapters.summary: Xanthe seeks out Ilsa Reyes, a retired river captain who once ran cargo for Vessani refugees and owes his mother a debt. She agrees to guide him upstream but insists they take her slow, armored barge, not the plane. POV: Ilsa. Beat: loyalty as inheritance; grudging alliance formed.

chapters.title: Departure Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Loading the barge under pretense of a supply run, Xanthe discovers his hangar searched and the chest's lock scratched. He moves the letters to a false fuel tank and burns a decoy envelope. POV: Xanthe. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve; point of no return.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: The barge fights the upper gorge; a winch line snaps and Ilsa nearly drowns saving the deck cargo. Working the lines together, Xanthe and Ilsa trade histories and something warmer kindles. POV: Ilsa. Beat: love beginning against both their rules.

chapters.title: The Plane That Follows
chapters.summary: Crane's chartered aircraft shadows them upriver; Xanthe uses fog and a dead-end tributary to lose it, cracking a float on rocks in the process. POV: Xanthe. Beat: cost of defiance mounting; the escape feels too easy.

chapters.title: Corben's Landing Burns
chapters.summary: A radio call brings terrible news: Miriam's archive has been torched and she's missing. The message includes coordinates—clearly bait meant for Xanthe. POV: Miriam, captive, then Xanthe receiving word. Beat: guilt ignites; the hunt turns personal.

chapters.title: The Toll of the Narrows
chapters.summary: At a fortified narrows, men flying no flag demand toll from all river traffic. Ilsa barges through using an old Vessani recognition sign—and the sentries' faces change: they know the name Okafor. POV: Ilsa. Beat: revelation that the drowned nation never fully died.

chapters.title: Settlement Above the Falls
chapters.summary: Beyond the falls lies New Vessa, a hidden town of descendants keeping the seal alive in secret. Elder Tomas Wren receives Xanthe coldly: heirs bring soldiers, and soldiers bring erasure. POV: Tomas. Beat: welcome laced with fear; Xanthe sees his mother's eyes in strangers.

chapters.title: His Mother's Room
chapters.summary: Shown the house his mother grew up in, Xanthe finds her girlhood diary confirming the treasury's vault beneath Cape Reckoning—and her reason for fleeing: she refused to let the elders use it as a bargaining chip. POV: Xanthe. Beat: understanding replaces resentment; theme of loyalty vs. truth deepens.

chapters.title: The Council of Kept Things
chapters.summary: New Vessa's council debates: surrender the letters to Crane's superiors for amnesty, or open the vault and risk everything. Xanthe argues for truth; Tomas argues for survival. The vote splits. POV: Tomas. Beat: the community fractures along the book's central fault line.

chapters.title: Crane Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Crane arrives with a gunboat and a warrant, but privately reveals his own secret: he is Vessani-born, raised to infiltrate and betray, and he wants the vault for himself. He gives Xanthe until dawn. POV: Crane. Beat: antagonist humanized; betrayal within betrayal.

chapters.title: Night Flight Over Black Water
chapters.summary: Xanthe repairs his floatplane with settlement help and flies reconnaissance over Cape Reckoning, mapping the gunboat and finding the sea-cave entrance to the vault. Ilsa navigates from the right seat. POV: Xanthe. Beat: love declared plainly between passes over black water.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Cape
chapters.summary: Xanthe, Ilsa, and Tomas enter the sea cave at low tide and open the vault: not gold, but the complete Vessani record—treaties, censuses, proof the dissolution decree was forged. Crane follows them in. POV: Xanthe. Beat: climax begins; the inheritance is truth itself.

chapters.title: Cape Reckoning
chapters.summary: Confrontation in the flooding cave: Crane holds them at gunpoint until Xanthe shows him his own family's names in the census. Shamed and unmoored, Crane hesitates; the tide forces everyone out as the gunboat shells the cape. POV: Crane. Beat: climax—loyalty vs. truth resolved in Crane's broken choice.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: The vault floods; the original documents are lost, but Xanthe had photographed every page during the night flight. Crane, wounded, orders the gunboat to stand down and takes the blame for the raid. POV: Xanthe. Beat: sacrifice and reversal—the chest is gone, the evidence survives.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the photographs reach courts and newspapers; the forged decree unravels and New Vessa's existence enters negotiation instead of erasure. Miriam, freed, testifies. Crane disappears upriver. POV: Miriam. Beat: falling action—truth costs much and buys a future.

chapters.title: Flight Plan, Filed Honestly
chapters.summary: Spring: Xanthe files his first flight plan under his full, true name, with Ilsa beside him and the settlement's charter tucked in the map case. The river forgives nothing, but he has stopped asking it to forget. POV: Xanthe. Beat: resolution—love, inheritance, and truth reconciled in one honest departure.
